summary.headline: Shelter Pharma FY26 revenue rose 44% to INR 73.13 Cr with PAT of INR 9.03 Cr; management targets INR 200 Cr revenue by FY2030.
summary.overview: Shelter Pharma reported FY26 revenue from operations of INR 73.13 Cr (up 44% YoY), EBITDA of INR 12.72 Cr (margin 17.39%, up 26% YoY) and PAT of INR 9.03 Cr (up 25% YoY). Q4 revenue was INR 39.84 Cr (up 50% YoY) and exports were about INR 6 Cr (up 164%). Management is expanding sales teams and distributors, which has compressed margins from roughly 20-21% in FY24-FY25, and working capital has stretched to 234 days with operating cash flow of minus INR 12.48 Cr. Management reiterated the INR 200 Cr FY2030 revenue target and outlined a second plant near Ahmedabad, with capex of about INR 12-15 Cr.

segments.name: Veterinary (animal health)
segments.commentary: About 55% of FY26 revenue. Leading products include Feedvet multivitamin powder, Lactocal calcium gel, Vymet D3+E liquid, Diarub bolus and Livodin liquid.

segments.name: Human healthcare
segments.commentary: About 45% of FY26 revenue. Key brands are Lemon & Barley Water (about INR 3.0-3.5 Cr revenue, no direct competition claimed), Sherolax, Gashoshel, Meryn, Joemega, All Vitamins and Omega-3 capsules. Management says human and veterinary margins are similar.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About INR 6 Cr in FY26, up 164%, mainly Africa and Middle East (UAE, Kuwait, Iraq, Qatar, Nepal, Bangladesh, Mauritius, Yemen, Sudan). Management says export margins are 20-25% higher than domestic; over INR 5 Cr already reached in Q1 FY27 per management.

guidance_outlook: Revenue target of about INR 200 Cr by FY2030, which management called 'actual numbers, not that conservative'.
Revenue mix goal of 40-45% human healthcare with similar margins.
EBITDA margin expected to stay around current levels (~17%) this year or next, then rise to 22-25% over the next two to three years; management said it will not go below 17%.
Working capital days to fall from 234 to about 60 and then to about one month; management says FY27 growth of about 40% CAGR is 'absolutely possible'.
Second plant installation to begin around end-2027 (approvals from December 2026), with capex of about INR 12-15 Cr mostly funded from internal accruals.
No plan to raise capital currently; company is debt-free and will rely on internal accruals.
capex_capacity: Existing Himatnagar plant closed FY26 at about INR 75 Cr revenue; management says it can reach INR 100 Cr on the same plant.
Land near Ahmedabad acquired for a second manufacturing facility for about INR 2.5 Cr, funded from internal accruals.
Second plant: installation to start around end-2027 after approvals from December 2026; estimated capex INR 12-15 Cr.
Team: about 80 in sales, 12 in Ahmedabad office and 50 in the factory; sales team expected to double in two years.
Distribution: 12,000+ doctors reached and 5,000+ retail pharmacies; coverage expanded from 10-12 states to 15+ states, pan-India by FY27 per management.
demand_pricing: Management says the Ayurvedic market (INR 1,070 bn in 2025 to INR 3,728 bn by 2034, 15.52% CAGR) supports growth; organised players dominate value.
Verka Dairy order: minimum order value about INR 1-1.5 Cr initially, per management.
Africa, Middle East and state-government and central procurement (KPKB, CGHS, CSD) applications are being pursued; management says each African container is worth about INR 1-1.5 Cr.
Government and bulk supply margins were not quantified; management says bulk purchasing is used to build stock.
Export order book size was not disclosed; management will follow up via Financial Minds.

qa_highlights.question: Why are loans and advances on the balance sheet, and what is the return?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said advances (about INR 37 Cr per an analyst's reading) are raw-material advances for long-term procurement and export pipeline orders; no return was specified.

qa_highlights.question: Why did promoter stake fall?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it was internal structuring: a family member was exiting part of the stake, and the promoter is buying stakes; not a promoter stake sale.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Middle East war hit margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pharma is treated as essential; three shipments are in transit to Africa and one to Dubai, with no margin impact expected.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 200 Cr target conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is realistic: exports were about INR 2.5 Cr in FY25 and about INR 6.5 Cr in FY26, with over INR 5 Cr already in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is planned for the next plant and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates INR 12-15 Cr, mostly from internal accruals, with installation starting around end-2027 after approvals from December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EBITDA margin down from about 20% to 17%, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the dip to aggressive expansion in sales teams, channels and distributors; margins expected to stay similar this year or next, then rise to 22-25% in two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow negative and working capital at 234 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it moved from advance payments in three states to credit terms in new states; credit days were cut from 120 to 90 and are targeted at 60, then about one month.

qa_highlights.question: Why was preference equity of INR 42.44 Cr issued?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was mainly for working capital to fund a sales team that is expected to double in the next two years.

risks_watch: Negative operating cash flow (INR -12.48 Cr) and 234-day working capital cycle; watch whether credit days fall toward 60.
EBITDA margin of 17.39% is below the FY24-FY25 level of about 20-21%; the target recovery to 22-25% depends on the expansion cost ramp fading.
Dependence on small orders (about INR 1-1.5 Cr per container or order); the INR 200 Cr FY30 target needs much larger order flow, and no large pipeline was disclosed.
Preference share issue of INR 42.44 Cr, which management says is for working capital; the equity dilution (about 40% per analyst) needs clarifying.
Export order book not disclosed; the Middle East conflict could affect shipments despite management's reassurance.
Inconsistent product and revenue figures in the call (e.g., FY25 export numbers, 200 vs 300 product counts, and the 'FY25' vs 'FY26' year label) warrant verification against filings.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansion-focused on growth and the FY30 target, but evasive on the order book, the preference share purpose and the stake change, and frequently offered general explanations rather than figures.
key_quotes: These are, I think, very actual numbers, not that conservative and not so aggressive.
So, there are no hurdles and there is no margin down or anything because of the war.
So, going forward, we are trying to reduce the days. It was —we, when we started, we were offering 120 days, then we reduced it to 90 days.
We hope so, yes. Of course.

adds.what: Second manufacturing plant near Ahmedabad (land acquired, installation after approvals from Dec 2026)

growth.why: Management targets ~INR 200 Cr revenue by FY2030 (vs FY26 INR 73 Cr), backed by existing Himatnagar plant able to reach INR 100 Cr, a second Ahmedabad plant (capex INR 12-15 Cr, install from end-2027), export order traction (Verka Dairy, Africa containers worth INR 1-1.5 Cr each) and sales/distribution expansion, but the export order book was not disclosed and the plant timeline is 2027+.
